title: HP Hampden X3027 - Relics
memorial_details:
description: Partial transcription from the display sheets: Propeller from Handley Page Hampden X3027/ On the night of the 27/28 October 1940;/ RAF Bomber Command tasked/ 82 aircraft across numerous targets in Germany and the Occupied/ Countries. At RAF Scampton, between 15:00 and 17:40 hrs 49 Squadron/ dispatched 8 Hampdens with 6 aircraft hitting the primary target of/ Hamburg and the remaining 2 bombing alternative targets. Squadron/ losses were limited to 1 damaged (X3001) and 1 shot down (X3027)/
 
Hampden X3001 (Pilot Officer Green and crew.) successfully located/ and bombed their allocated target but on return to Lincolnshire and/ whilst orbiting RAF Scampton's Q Site (the decoy flarepath at Rand) was/ 
attacked by a nightfighter of 2/NJG2 flown by Leutnant Heinz Völker./ The Hampden suffered slight(!) damage including 3 burst tyres and shot/ accumulators, but landed safely at 01:25 hrs./ 

It is reported that Hampden X3027, with one engine out of action, was/ heard to circle Skegness before, it is believed, attempting to ditch in the/ sea in shallow water close to shore./ At 02:00 hrs the Lifeboat Hon. Secretary, Mr H E Sparrow, received a/ telephone message from the Skegness Coastguard that an aircraft was/ down just North of the pier and that cries for help could clearly be/ heard. [Partial transcript form the information sheets on the associated display board].
